name: Tiarere Lussan
about: Born and raised in Tahiti, I left for Paris at 18 to join the ENS D2 preparatory class at Lycée Turgot: two intensive years of microeconomics, macroeconomics, economic history and mathematics. I then completed a final year of Economics at Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne before joining EDHEC Business School, where I am now in the first year of the Master in Management.

Alongside my studies, I am an audit intern at Gatti Conseil, where I work on the statutory audit of a group of 40+ entities and built AI agents that cut a key audit test from nine hours to about two. Before that, my path took me from grading Tahitian pearls for an international clientele to analysing global markets for Tahiti Tourisme and building business partnerships in Silicon Valley. What connects it all is a love of craft, culture and the people behind them, and the conviction that great objects deserve great stories.
I am now looking for two six-month internships in New York, at the meeting point of art, luxury and technology.

projects.title: AI agents for audit testing
projects.summary: 18 AI agents that automate the sales-accuracy tests of a financial audit: 50 tests go from 9 hours by hand to about 2 hours — 4 to 5 times faster. Built in my first three weeks at Gatti Conseil.
projects.description:
During my audit internship at Gatti Conseil, I automated the accuracy tests on a client's sales listing (IPE): checking that every sampled sale is backed by its invoice, quote or work order, and intervention report.

What I built:
— Ready-to-use Excel template sheets with built-in formulas and colour-coded conclusions.
— 18 AI agents in DataSnipper: one checks that every document is present and correctly named, others extract invoices, quotes and intervention reports into the tables, each extraction is cross-checked by a second agent, and the last ones draft the conclusion comments and the list of documents to request from the client.
— A step-by-step guide so that anyone on the team can run the test, even without prior DataSnipper experience.

Result: a batch of 50 tests took a colleague 9 hours by hand; with the agents it takes about 2 hours, review included — roughly 7 hours saved per company audited, 4 to 5 times faster (initial estimate, documents already retrieved; timing on upcoming engagements in progress).

The AI does the reading and the checks; the auditor validates every entry and draws the conclusions. Every value stays linked to the exact spot on the source document, and the use of AI is documented for reviewers.

Client data is confidential and not shown here.

projects.title: Tahitian pearls, from lagoon to client
projects.summary: Three weeks inside the full life cycle of a Tahitian pearl on Taha'a: lagoon work, harvest, grading and luxury retail.
projects.description:
At Love Here Pearl Farm, I lived on site and took part in every stage of production.

How a Tahitian pearl is made
— Pearl oysters (Pinctada margaritifera) come from the Tuamotu Islands. A grafter inserts a mother-of-pearl nucleus and a piece of mantle tissue: the most delicate step, which triggers the layering of nacre.
— The oysters hang vertically on ropes and nets in the lagoon, identified by numbered buoys and cleaned every three months.
— The first harvest comes after 12 to 18 months; an oyster can be regrafted up to three times over about seven years.

What I did
— Attached oysters to the lines and dived to secure them underwater.
— Harvested the pearls and learned to grade them: top gem, A to E, shapes from round to baroque, and keshi, pure nacre pearls formed without a nucleus.
— Sold them to luxury cruise passengers on a private motu.

What I took away: a pearl's value is built through authenticity, storytelling and rarity. That conviction is what draws me to the meeting point of art, culture and business, from fine jewellery to auction houses.

projects.title: Strategic analysis for Tahiti Tourisme
projects.summary: A strategic and budget review of how The Islands of Tahiti are promoted abroad, with recommendations on positioning, internal operations and seasonality.
projects.description:
During my internship in the International Operations Department, I prepared a strategic analysis for Tahiti Tourisme's 2025 promotion.

What it covers
— Budget allocation: how the promotion budget is split across 13 international markets and eight types of activities, from B2B trade work to brand campaigns and consumer events.
— Target segments by market: luxury and eco-responsible travellers in Australia and New Zealand, couples in Europe and the United States, seniors in Japan and Korea.
— A SWOT of tourism in French Polynesia: a unique natural and cultural heritage and no mass tourism, against high prices, dependence on a few markets and a perception centred on Bora Bora.
— Seasonality: using public data from the Polynesian statistics institute (ISPF, 2018–2025), a month-by-month potential matrix for each market, to target the low season.

My recommendations
— Compete on differentiation, not price, and keep one stable brand message built around mana, the Polynesian notion of spiritual energy.
— Promote cultural and regenerative tourism, and open new segments such as business events (MICE).
— Simplify internal operations: fewer, longer campaigns, aligned holiday calendars for every market, and fewer tools and procedures.

projects.title: Turgot Alumni
projects.summary: Alumni directory and website for the Lycée Turgot preparatory-class network, where I serve as vice-president.
projects.description:
As vice-president of the association, I designed and built its website from scratch: a React site deployed on Vercel, connected to a Supabase database that powers the alumni directory.

Features: alumni sign-up, a member area where alumni log in and edit their own profile, an admin area to approve and manage entries, email notifications, GDPR consent, and searchable orientation sheets and testimonials for current preparatory-class students.

The association connects more than 500 former students of the Lycée Turgot preparatory classes across five tracks. Its site offers 100+ orientation sheets written by alumni, a searchable directory and live testimonials.

I also run the association's social media and its annual orientation forum.

projects.title: Vive les Vacances !
projects.summary: Lead photographer, fundraising and tutoring for a charity of 40 EDHEC student volunteers that takes children from the Lille area on holiday.
projects.description:
Vive les Vacances ! is run by about 40 EDHEC student volunteers in Roubaix. It gives children aged 6 to 13 from the Lille area monthly outings, daily homework help and holidays.

My role
— Lead photographer: I cover the association's main events, such as the multi-sport games, the Christmas show and the spring holidays, and produce its visual communication.
— Fundraising: I answer calls for projects to finance the children's holidays and help maintain relations with partners.
— Weekly tutoring for children from the local social centres.

The association's results include more than 4,000 toys collected and handed out to 1,500 children, about 100 children sent on spring holidays and 140 at the children's multi-sport games.
